title: Competency Maps and Rotation Paths
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Title: Competency Maps and Rotation Paths

Summary:
This playbook defines Redwood’s competency maps for core functions, the formal rotation program for cross-team experience, and the operational procedures for role transitions and temporary assignments. It is intended for ICs, managers, and people-ops partners who coordinate career development and resourcing.

Scope:
- Applies to all full-time and fixed-term employees at Redwood in engineering, product, research, and go-to-market teams.
- Excludes executive-level strategic reassignments (handled by People & the relevant executive sponsor).

Goals:
1. Provide clear, measurable competency definitions per band to reduce ambiguity during promotions and rotations.
2. Enable safe, low-friction rotations that grow skills and spread institutional knowledge.
3. Standardize approvals, duration, and success metrics for temporary assignments.

Audience:
- Individual contributors (IC1–IC5)
- Engineering and product managers
- People-ops and hiring managers

Contents:
1) Competency map overview
2) Rotation program (process + cadence)
3) Request & approval workflow (step-by-step)
4) Onboarding/exit checklist for rotations
5) Metrics and post-rotation evaluation
6) Tools and access instructions
7) FAQs and examples

---

1) Competency map overview
Each role family uses a 5-band map (T-shaped skills + leadership behaviors). Minimum expectations are listed below; managers should use these as the basis for calibration conversations.

Table: Core example — Software Engineering (short form)
| Band | Scope & Impact | Typical Responsibilities | Success signals (measurable) |
|------|----------------|--------------------------|------------------------------|
| IC1  | Component-level | Fix bugs, deliver small features | PR lead-time < 3 days, passes unit tests, peer reviews OK |
| IC2  | Service-level   | Own small service modules, stable delivery | Leads 2 small projects per quarter, <2 regressions per release |
| IC3  | System-level    | Design cross-service features, mentor IC1/IC2 | Design docs reused, uptime metrics met (>=99.9%) |
| IC4  | Domain-level    | Influence roadmap, run postmortems, shape hiring | Drives 1+ major initiative, reduces unit cost by measurable % |
| IC5  | Company-level   | Technical strategy, external representation | Drives long-term platform roadmap, successful cross-org programs |

Competency dimensions (applies across families):
- Technical craft (depth & scalability)
- Execution & delivery (quality, speed, incident behavior)
- Collaboration & influence (cross-team impact, mentoring)
- Product judgment & customer orientation
- Operational ownership (SLOs, runbooks, paged support)

Calibration guidance:
- Use quarterly calibration docs. Promotion packet should include: 2–3 peer reviews, 1 manager narrative, 2-3 artifact examples (design docs, metrics) and a 90-day impact summary if promoted within the last year.

---

2) Rotation program (purpose, types, and durations)
Purpose: Rotations accelerate learning, reduce bus factor, and surface transferable skills for future leadership. Redwood supports two rotation types:
- Short rotations (3 months): Skill-focused shadowing or feature sprint participation.
- Long rotations (6–12 months): Full responsibility for a role-equivalent scope; suitable for stretch assignments.

Eligibility:
- Minimum six months in current role unless waived by manager + people-ops for critical hires.
- Manager concurrence required.
- Role backfill plan for the sending team must be defined for long rotations.

Constraints:
- No more than 10% of a single team headcount can be on long rotations simultaneously.
- A single employee may not do back-to-back long rotations without a 3-month stabilization period.

---

3) Request & approval workflow (numbered steps)
1. Nomination: Employee or manager opens a Rotation Request in People Portal (see Tools). Include: desired role, target manager, duration, learning goals, and backfill plan if needed.
2. Manager review: Sending manager verifies impact and suggests mitigation plan within 5 business days.
3. Receiving manager assessment: Confirms scope, success metrics, and onboarding plan within 5 business days.
4. People-ops approval: Confirms policy constraints and approves on platform (2 business days).
5. Handover window: 1–2 weeks for knowledge transfer.
6. Rotation start: Employee begins in receiving team. People-ops creates temporary reporting and access changes.
7. Midpoint check-in: Formal check at 1/2 duration with manager + people-ops to confirm progress.
8. Exit & evaluation: Final review, artifact handoff, and capture of lessons learned in the Rotation Retrospective template.

Decision criteria for approval:
- Keeps team delivery within SLO targets (engineering SLOs): e.g., release cadence & incident response not materially impacted.
- Clear learning outcomes tied to competencies.
- Backfill or mitigation approved for long rotations.

---

4) Onboarding and exit checklist (for rotations)
Onboarding checklist (to be completed by receiving manager):
- Invite to team channels & calendar shared.
- Assign buddy and 30/60/90 plan.
- Grant required access: repo, CI, issue tracker (list below).
- Define initial deliverables and success metrics.

Exit checklist (to be completed by sending manager + employee):
- Transfer documentation (runbooks, pending PRs, configs).
- Update ownership matrix (RACI).
- Capture debrief: 30–45 minute guided retro stored in People Portal.

Templates: See Rotation Retrospective template in People Portal (link ID: ROT-RETRO).

---

5) Metrics and post-rotation evaluation
Key metrics to capture per rotation (people-ops will surface aggregate trends quarterly):
- Learning outcomes met (binary + qualitative)
- Time-to-onboard (days to first meaningful contribution)
- Impact on sending team delivery (delta vs baseline)
- Retention & engagement signals (e.g., pulse survey score change)

Post-rotation review artifacts (required):
- Manager evaluation (form)
- Employee self-eval (form)
- 1–2 artifacts demonstrating impact (e.g., PRs, cost savings, docs)

---

6) Tools and access instructions
Primary tools used during the rotation program:
- People Portal (https://people.redwood.internal): submit rotation request, view status, access templates. CLI: people-cli rotation submit --role \"backend-engineer\" --target-manager \"@jordan\" --duration 3m
- Identity & Access (IAM console): receiving manager requests repos and service access via the IAM ticket form.
- Team calendar & Slack: channels for onboarding. Use /rotation-start in #people-ops to signal start to the org.
- Knowledge repo: team-runbooks, architecture docs in Redwood Docs (search: rotation on-boarding).

Access timeline expectations:
- Basic repo access: within 2 business days of start.
- Elevated infra access (production): requires 5 business days and buddy-approved training.

---

7) FAQs and examples
Q: Can a contractor participate in rotations?
A: Contractors may participate in short rotations with manager + people-ops approval; long rotations require contract amendment.

Q: Does a rotation count as a promotion opportunity?
A: Rotations are development experiences. Promotions follow the standard promotion packet & calibration process and are independent of rotation status, though rotation artifacts may support promotion evidence.

Example: Backend->Infra short rotation (3 months)
- Goal: learn deployment orchestration and reduce average model cold-start by 20%
- Success metrics: deploy automation that reduces manual deploy steps by 40% and a PR with end-to-end tests merged
- Midpoint check-in: demonstration of CI pipeline changes

---

Ownership and governance
- Program owner: People-ops (primary), partnered with Eng Managers Forum for operational guardrails.
- Quarterly review: People-ops publishes a Rotation Program dashboard with utilization, success rates, and business impact.

Operational KPIs (tracked by people-ops):
- Rotation acceptance rate (%)
- Median time-to-approval (days)
- Post-rotation success rate (manager+employee agreement)

Change process
- Policy updates follow standard Confluence change workflow: proposed -> in_review by People-ops + Eng Managers -> published. Significant changes must be communicated two weeks prior to taking effect.

Appendices
A. Rotation request form field definitions (extract)
- Desired role: free text (title + key responsibilities)
- Duration: select (3m, 6m, 12m)
- Learning goals: up to 5 bullets
- Success metrics: up to 5 measurable outcomes
- Backfill plan: names + mitigation steps

B. Related templates and links
- Promotion packet checklist: /confluence/company-handbook/02_roles-and-career/promotion-packet-checklist
- Rotation Retrospective (ROT-RETRO): People Portal template

C. Example 6-month rotation schedule (week-by-week highlights)
- Weeks 1–2: onboarding, know-your-tools
- Weeks 3–8: feature sprint, weekly demos
- Weeks 9–20: ownership period, independent deliverables
- Weeks 21–24: handback + retrospective

Contact
For questions or to propose an exception, open a ticket with People-ops (people-ops@redwood.internal) or post in #people-ops.
